more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
more_info.overview: Cochineal extract and carmine are red colours whose main pigment is carminic acid. Carmine is a metal complex made from that pigment. In foods these materials produce red shades. The specified material is supplied as deep red powder or liquid.
more_info.origin: Animal-derived, specifically from dried female cochineal insects. Extraction releases carminic acid; reaction with aluminium forms carmine, sometimes with other metal ions.
more_info.daily_intake: 2.5 mg carminic acid/kg body weight per day (EFSA, 2015). This expresses the earlier 5 mg carmine/kg body weight ADI in terms of carminic acid content.
more_info.side_effects:
At food-use levels, allergic reactions to cochineal/carmine can occur; EFSA could not establish a threshold dose for allergy. Residual proteins were identified as a reason to improve purification.
The animal toxicity studies reviewed by EFSA did not justify lowering the existing ADI; this does not remove the separate allergy risk.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured drinks; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; unripened cheese excluding products falling in category 16.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: Not suitable for vegan or vegetarian diets because the colour is extracted from insects.
more_info.precautions: EFSA identified allergenic material in E120 and recommended manufacturing purification steps because no allergy threshold could be established.
